newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Aug construction spending rose 0.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Aug construction spending rose 0.9 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department seasonally adjusted construction spending, with comparisons.
PERCENT CHANGES: Aug July--Rev from Aug96/95
ANNUAL RATES, BILLIONS OF U.S. DOLLARS: Aug'95
ANNUAL RATES, BILLIONS OF U.S. DOLLARS:
PERCENT CHANGES: Aug July--Rev from Aug96/95
Wall Street economists expected a 0.8 percent rise in August construction spending.
Construction spending in 1992 dollars, which discounts the effects of inflation:
Annual Rates, Billions of U.S. Dollars --
Private nonresidential spending, which hit a $139.5 billion annual rate in August, was the highest on record, the department said.
Public construction spending fell for a third straight month in August.

The department revised June construction spending to a 0.8 percent rise from a 0.7 percent increase. It revised June private construction spending to up 1.2 percent from a 1.1 percent rise and June public spending to a 0.3 percent decrease from down 0.5 percent.
